title: Maximum Cost of Trip With K Highways
summary: Given a network of n cities connected by highways, where each highway has a toll cost, find the maximum cost of a trip that crosses exactly k highways.
statement: Given a network of n cities connected by highways, where each highway has a toll cost, find the maximum cost of a trip that crosses exactly k highways. You can start at any city and visit each city at most once. If no such trip exists, return -1.
constraints: Highways are undirected weighted edges between distinct cities.
A trip crosses exactly k highways and may visit each city at most once; it may start anywhere.
Return the maximum toll sum or -1 if no such simple trip exists.
hints: The visited-city set and current endpoint completely describe what extensions remain legal.
Store the best cost for each (bitmask,last city), starting with every one-city trip.
Repeat k times: extend along an edge only to an unvisited city and maximize the new state.
Each transition appends one distinct city and one highway; after k layers the states are exactly all legal trips of the required length.
editorial: Each transition appends one distinct city and one highway; after k layers the states are exactly all legal trips of the required length.
